messages.subject: Missing areas
parts:
Hello group,

I am working with several communities that are collaborating to monitor an endangered grizzly population. The overall density is approximately 2.8 bears/1000km2. From previous research, I know that the approximate female and male sigma is 3.91km and 11.48 km respectively and that the population is small and isolated. 

The current project is ongoing and they are planning to sample every second year. After their first year, in 2019, it seems as though the sampling is somewhat uneven (see image below), and there are a few "holes" and areas with lower sampling intensity. They did 4 occasions at each site in 2019 and plan to repeat in 2021. 

I am curious whether the group thinks it would be worth it to sample the "holes" in 2020 and add this as an additional set of occasions/session? Or to leave it and conduct a more thorough sampling effort in 2021?

Background: The area of interest is north of the scale bar (North is the top of the page). Adult females' home ranges from a few telemetered bears are outlined in thin lines. In 2005 there were a few individuals in the thicker red area, while no bears were detected in the blue. In 2019 There were no grizzlies detected in most southern sites (larger green dots).
